draft.title: Trees
card: A network is connected if there is a route between every pair of vertices.
A tree is a connected network that contains no circuits. Take away any one edge and it is no longer connected.
A tree with n vertices has n − 1 edges. Example: a tree with 6 vertices has 6 − 1 = 5 edges.
To test a network, check that it is connected and has no circuits. If a connected network has n vertices and more than n − 1 edges, it must contain a circuit, so it is not a tree.
draft.remember: A tree is connected with no circuits, and n vertices means n − 1 edges.

a.q: A tree has 12 vertices. How many edges does it have?
a.why: A tree with n vertices has n − 1 edges, so 12 − 1 = 11. Choosing 12 mixes up the number of edges with the number of vertices.
a.clue: Take one away from the number of vertices.

b.q: A council plans a walking track network joining 7 lookouts around Bendigo. It has 7 vertices, is connected and has 7 edges. Is it a tree?
opts: No, because a tree would have only 6 edges
Yes, because it has as many edges as vertices
No, because a tree would have 8 edges
b.why: A tree with 7 vertices has 7 − 1 = 6 edges. This network has one extra edge, so it must contain a circuit. Being connected is not enough, because a tree also needs no circuits.
b.clue: Work out how many edges a tree with 7 vertices has, then compare.

b.best: No, because a tree would have only 6 edges
